2. Opposite party No. 1 and Abdul Majid Predecessor of opposite party Nos. 2-13 as plaintiffs filed on 1.12.62 Title Suit No. 176 of 1962 against the petitioner and another for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in the suit property measuring .22 acres of plot No. 372/1065 of khatian No. 614 situated within Kalitala of Dinajpur town with structures standing thereon and the said suit subsequently was re-numbered as Title Suit No. 367 of 1968. 

 12. Before parting with the judgment it is necessary to consider an intricate question of law as to whether a co-sharer can recover possession of the property from a trespasser, Court of appeal below on consideration of deed of gift Ext. 8, municipal assessment registers Ext. 'L' series and CS Khatian Ext. E (3) recording suit property in the possession of Prova Rani found that Shyama Pada Chakravorty and Prova Rani acquired right, title and possession in the suit property. Admittedly Shyamapada Chakravorty did not execute the power of attorney Ext. 'I' on the basis of which the deed of exchange kabala Ext.2 was executed and registered. Court of appeal below obviated this difficulty by noticing that Shyama Pada Chakarborty did not challenge plaintiffs' claim of title in the entire suit property in spite of being impleaded and served with summons of the suit. Even if it is found that plaintiffs acquired title of Prova Rani only on the basis of Ext. l and 2 in the suit premises defendant petitioner having been found to be a rank trespasser in the suit premises and he having not acquired any title by adverse possession plaintiffs are entitled to recover khas possession of the suit premises by evicting the petitioner. In this respect reliance can be made in the cases of Md. Abdur Rahman Bhuiyan vs. Prajulla Chandra Majumdar reported in PLD 1963 (Dhaka) 57; Fazal Hussain vs. Noor Khan reported in PLD 1957 (Lah) 43; Ram Charan vs. Bansidhar and others reported in AIR 1942 (All) 358 and RN Das vs. Loknath Mandai reported in AIR 1970 Patna l (FB). In the aforesaid cases it has been consistently held that a suit at the instance of a co-sharer against a trespasser for recovery of possession is maintainable without even impleading the other co-sharers. In this case after remand Shyama Pada Chakraborty was impleaded and it has already been noticed that he did not contest the claim of the plaintiffs. Vested property authority and Government also did not contest the claim of the plaintiffs though impleaded in this suit. In the above facts and circumstances I find no illegality in the impugned judgment and decree to interfere with the same.
